In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of strong nuclear magnetic fields in molecules, and their experimental monitoring.
the following: (1) the theory of pseudorotating molecules, (2) the excitation of the pseudorotations by a laser pulse and (3) the strong nuclear ring currents and induced magnetic fields.
the design of strong electric ring currents and magnetic ring fields, which may be used for the design of novel nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) techniques.

the strong nuclear ring currents and induced magnetic fields are the first example of the general phenomenon of nuclear excitations in pseudorotations.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of pseudorotation, a molecule can be induced to carry a nuclear ring current and magnetic field.
a strong magnetic field can be induced by a strong nuclear ring current in molecules, without the need to pre-align the molecules.
the strong magnetic field can be produced in a molecule without a permanent magnetic moment, by a circularly-polarized laser field.
